entities.summary: Saint Æbbe of Coldingham, also known as Æbbe the Younger, was an Abbess of Coldingham Priory in south-east Scotland. She played a crucial role in the Christianization of the region, which was heavily influenced by the Viking invasions of the 9th century. Æbbe's leadership and diplomacy helped to establish the Coldingham Priory as a center of learning and spirituality, attracting scholars and pilgrims from across Europe. The priory's scriptorium produced several illuminated manuscripts, including the Lindisfarne Gospels, which showcased the region's unique artistic style. Æbbe's legacy extends beyond her religious endeavors, as she was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the local economy. Her influence can be seen in the development of the Scottish monastic tradition and the preservation of Celtic culture. The Coldingham Priory's ruins still stand today, a testament to Æbbe's enduring impact on Scottish history.
